messages:
mike: incident-bot just fired a page for tenant `nova` on reserved pool `reserved-nyc-2`. p95 latency > 4s and ~12% 5xx from that tenant. PagerDuty notification went out.

oncall-bot: PAGE FIRED - Severity P1 - nova: reserved-pool-saturation (pagerduty://INC12345)

pagerduty: PagerDuty alert created: INC12345 - nova reserved pool high latency. On-call: mike

mike: acked on PD. Quick status: traffic for nova spiked ~3x after a customer rollout. Autoscaler did not add reserved nodes due to a config bug (min=0). Looks like warmup + KV cache misses cause spike in GPU usage.

tara: copying logs — seeing lots of `KV_CACHE_MISS` and `model_host` OOMs on a subset of instances. Would adding burst capacity help short-term?

jess: @tara can you post the kv/cache logs snippet? also what does the reserved pool show in the console?

alex: console shows pool `reserved-nyc-2` at 100% queued, backend instances at ~98% GPU util. Autoscale policy for reserved pools has `min_replicas: 0` (🤦). It should be 2 for customer-facing dedicated pools.

chen: that's the rollout config bug we've seen in staging. We have a hotfix branch to enforce `min_replicas >= 2` for reserved pools.

jess: mitigation plan (short): 1) temporarily enable burst capacity for nova, 2) manually bump reserved pool replicas to +3, 3) route nova traffic to fallback model variant (lower memory/latency) while we stabilize.

mike: performing step 1 now. Command: ```redwoodctl pools burst --pool reserved-nyc-2 --amount 3 --reason "nova spike"```

oncall-bot: ACTION: burst request accepted, provisioning 3 extra nodes (eta ~45s)

mike: done, ran `kubectl scale deploy/reserved-nyc-2 --replicas=6 -n dedicated` as well to be safe (had to wait for GPU image pull).

tara: logs during scale: ```[2026-08-12T21:13:05Z] model_host[pid=1124]: KV_CACHE_MISS key=usr:tx:uuid.. ttl=0
[2026-08-12T21:13:38Z] autoscaler: failed to respect min_replicas=0 -> requested replicas ignored
[2026-08-12T21:14:11Z] scheduler: queued tasks drained -> scheduling to new node
```

alex: after scale, p95 dropped from 4.2s -> 1.1s for nova within ~70s. 5xx rate decreased from 12% -> 1.6%. Still seeing a handful of OOMs on the old variant.

jess: running fallback routing to `gptx-small-quant` for nova for non-critical routes. Command: ```redwoodctl route set --tenant nova --route default --model gptx-small-quant --policy fallback-temp```

mike: applied fallback routing. Traffic split 80/20 (regular/fallback) to limit quality regressions. Monitoring now.

chen: pushed hotfix PR to enforce `min_replicas >= 2` for reserved pools: PR https://git.internal/redwood/infra/commit/7890ab. Can we roll that to prod after mitigation?

tara: yes please. Also want to run a one-off job to pre-warm KV cache for nova to prevent next spike: `redwoodctl cache prewarm --tenant nova --keys recent_tokens --parallel 8`.

mike: doing prewarm. ETA ~2m.

oncall-bot: NOTE: pagerduty INC12345 acknowledged by mike at 21:15 UTC

pagerduty: Incident INC12345 -> Status: acknowledged. Next escalation at 21:30 if not resolved.

alex: quick customer impact blurb: "From 21:10–21:20 UTC, customer tenant 'nova' experienced elevated latencies (p95 up to 4s) and increased 5xx (~12%). Mitigation (burst capacity + manual scale + fallback routing) reduced errors to ~1.6% and p95 ~1.1s by 21:17 UTC. Root cause: autoscaler config allowed min_replicas=0 for reserved pools; combined with a customer rollout causing cold KV cache storms."

jess: parallel tasks: - chen to merge + deploy min_replicas hotfix - tara to validate prewarm succeeded and monitor 5xx - mike to update PD incident and move to 'monitoring' once stable - alex to run post-incident capacity audit for reserved-nyc-2

chen: merging PR now. Will trigger infra deploy; ETA 8–12m.

tara: prewarm complete, logs show cache hit rate rising to 92% for nova queries. No new OOMs observed on newly booted nodes.

mike: updating PD summary and setting to monitoring. PD note: mitigation applied, looking for 15m stable window before close.

pagerduty: INC12345 -> Status: monitoring (updated by mike)

alex: doing audit, will post numbers in ~10m. Early look: reserved-nyc-2 had 1 node offline (image pull stuck) and autoscaler mis-evaluated load due to stale metric tags. Fixing metric tag parsing in a follow-up.

jess: handoff: i'm taking the next hour covering the tail end of this. If anything re-triggers, ping me@jess and i'll page PD. Otherwise we'll update postmortem with timeline + action items: (1) enforce min_replicas, (2) add prewarm job to rollout checklist, (3) add metric tag guardrails, (4) improve pager thresholds for reserved pools.

mike: thanks all. closing internal oncall thread after 30m stable. Good catch. :thumbsup: 

oncall-bot: THREAD CLOSED: monitoring -> resolved pending 30m stable window"
